output.brief: The write-off jump is mainly an internal problem, not a Haverlow problem. Since late July the night receiving team went from six to four people. Night pallets now wait about 3 h 52 min, up from 44 min, on an unrefrigerated dock that averages 15–17°C. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day-shift rates barely moved. Haverlow's trailer data show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened, so the 6.5–8°C receipt probe readings were taken after the product had warmed on the dock. The chambers are holding temperature. I am fairly confident (about 85%). Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Restore night staffing, or otherwise get pallets into the chambers quickly. Set a maximum dock-to-chamber time and track it weekly from scan data. Keep the receiving probe in place. Separately, Corriebank's easier credit rules coincide with higher credits, but whether over-claiming is happening is unproven. Pull a sample of their claims and check them against delivery lots before changing their terms.
